sentences.text: Respondents Date of Institution : 17.09.2022 Date of Arguments : 12.08.2024 Date of pronouncement : 12.08.2024  AWAR D 1.
This is claim petition u/s 164 of M.V. Act seeking for compensation on no fault liability in respect of death of late Chedi Mukhiya s/o Shibu Mukhiya in a road side accident occurred on 13.07.2022.

As per the averments on 13.07.2022 deceased was going on MACT No.484/2022 by SHAILENDER Page 1 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.08.12 17:03:40 +0530 motorcycle no.DL-5SCU-9535 stated to be on correct side of the road, following traffic rules.
However deceased while riding on that motorcycle, when reached near bus stop of Shrestha Vihar, met with an accident, resultantly he suffered fatal injuries.
In respect of an accident FIR No.335/2022 was registered at PS Aman Vihar u/s 279/304A IPC.
It is mentioned that respondent no.1 is the insurer and respondent no.2 is the owner of above said motorcycle.
A lump sum amount of compensation of Rs.5 lakhs as provided u/s 164 of M.V. Act has been sought in respect of the accident.

sentences.text: 1 2. Respondent no.1/insurer of motorcycle no.DL-5SCU-9535 has filed the WS taking an objection that claim petition u/s 164 M.V. Act is not maintainable as the petition does not fulfill the statutory requirement.

It is pleaded that insurance is not liable to indemnify because the liability to indemnify third party only arises whereas deceased himself was driving the vehicle in question and therefore liability of insurance does not arise.
Other averments of claim petition except the fact motorcycle in question was insured with respondent no.1 under the policy no. 2312910178783300000 has not been disputed.

3. Respondent no.2/owner of the above mentioned motorcycle has not disputed the fact that deceased Chedi Mukhiya died while driving motorcycle in question no.DL-5SCU-9535 which was owned by respondent no.2.
It is stated that there is no breach of insurance policy, therefore insurance company is liable to pay the compensation.

4. On the basis of pleadings and the peculiar issue arose in the present claim petition, this Tribunal on 22.02.2024 framed following issues :
(1)Whether the petitioner is entitled for the amount of MACT No.484/2022 by SHAILENDER Page 2 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.08.12 17:03:48 +0530 compensation in terms of Section 164 of M.V. Act, if so, for what amount?
(2)Relief.
5.
Petitioner, wife of the deceased Chhedi Mukhiya, namely Smt.Hira Devi has appeared in the witness box as PW1.
On behalf of Respondent no.2/insurance company one witness R1W1 Simranjeet Kaur has been examined.
6. I have heard Sh.Madhur Goel, ld. Counsel for petitioner as well as Sh.Rohit Sehrawat and Sh.Amit Tomar, ld. Counsels for respondent no.1/insurance.
I have also gone through the written submissions filed by ld. Counsels for the parties.
Issue No.1 7.

While deciding the question of compensation under Section 164 M.V. Act, this Tribunal need not to go into the question of rash and negligent driving as claim is based on the premise of 'no fault liability' as provided under the statute.
It is not disputed fact that deceased Chedi Mukhiya has died in a road side accident while driving motorcycle no.DL- 5SCU-9535

. Only issue for consideration is that insurance company is denying the liability on the ground that there was no third party loss as deceased himself was driving the motorcycle no.DL-5SCU-9535.
8.

Ld. Counsel for petitioner has submitted that even if the deceased was driving the motorcycle, he would still be entitled for compensation under Section 164 of M.V. Act as for all intents and purposes he would be considered to be 'third party'.

Counsel for the petitioner further submitted that a circular has been issued by IRDAI directing all the insurance companies in motor insurance business, requiring compulsory personal accident cover for the owner/driver of the vehicle.

There is no requirement in section 164 for third party liability coverage as is required in terms of section 163A M.V. Act before amendment.

Therefore there cannot be any parity of section 163A and 164 of M.V.
Act.
Counsel in this regard relies upon the judgment of Punjab & Haryana High Court in United India Insurance Company Limited vs. Bhateli Devi (FAO No.7450/2014 decided on 15.05.2023).

sentences.text: I have also gone through the written submissions filed on behalf of insurance company/R1.

It is submitted by counsel for respondent no.1 that since the owner of the motorcycle no.DL-5SCU-9535 was riding it at the time of accident, therefore he cannot be considered to be entitled for third party risk even for the purpose of claim u/s 164 M.V. Act.

Reliance is placed on judgment of Delhi High Court in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Prem and others (MAC Appeal No.540/2012 decided on 16.01.2015 ), Supreme Court judgment in Ningamma and others vs. United India Insurance Company 2009 ACJ 2020 (SC).

sentences.text: 10. Having considered the submissions and also going through the evidence, it be noted that sub-section (1) of Section 149 casts a liability upon the insurer to pay to the person entitled to the benefit of the decree "as if he was the judgment debtor", that is, the Statute raises a legal fiction to MACT No.484/2022 by SHAILENDER Page 4 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.08.12 17:04:03 +0530 the effect that for the said purpose the insurer would be deemed to be a judgment-debtor in respect of the liability of the insurer in respect of third party risks.

There is no exhaustive definition of 'third party' in Section 145 of the Act and the definition appearing in Section 145(i) is only inclusive; yet there may not be any difficulty in discerning the expression "third party",
as contemplated by the legislature, in that, the Policy of Insurance being an agreement between first and the second party, i.e., the insurer and the insured, rest all others, who suffer because of the use of Motor Vehicles, and whose risks, would fall within the definition of a third party.

The third party includes persons who suffer loss or damage, by use of a Motor Vehicle, either as occupants thereof,
while traveling on the road, or in any other vehicle.
11.

Other than the contracting parties to the insurance policy, the expression "third party" therefore,
should include everyone, be it a person traveling in another vehicle, one walking on the road or a passenger in the car itself which is the subject matter of the insurance policy.
Every insured takes out an insurance policy against a third-party risk.
It enters into a contract with the insurer, only with the motive, intention, and purpose of covering the risks which may arise in relation to claims lodged against him by a third party.
By agreeing to issue the insurance policy, the insurer undertakes to insure the insured and indemnify him against all risks and concerning all claims lodged against him by third parties.

Narrowing the concept, scope, and ambit of a third party, and therefore, excluding the passengers in the vehicle from its operation and purview would not only defeat the very purpose of taking out the insurance policy but the very object of the Motor Vehicles Act which makes it a Hira Devi vs Hdfc Ergo General Insurance Co. sentences.text: MACT No.484/2022 SHAILENDER Page 5 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.08.12 17:04:10 +0530 against third party risks.
12. However, only question in this context to examine is whether the driver of a vehicle who died in an accident was the owner of the vehicle or not.
Because if he himself is the owner of a vehicle obviously he cannot be considered to be a 'third-party' as discussed above.

In the case of Ningamma and others v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd. (supra) and New India Assurance Co. Ltd. V.
Sadanand Mukhi (2009) 2 SCC 417, the Supreme Court has held that the owner of the vehicle or his legal representatives or the borrower of the vehicle cannot raise a claim for an accident in which there was no negligence on the part of the insured vehicle.

entities.text: Ningamma and others v. United India Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
New India Assurance Co. Ltd. V.
Sadanand Mukhi (2009) 2 SCC 417
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that in the aforesaid decisions, Apex Court has held that the borrower of the vehicle steps into the shoes of the owner and, therefore, the borrower of the vehicle or his legal representatives are not entitled to compensation from the insurer under the Act.
It is submitted that the deceased in the present case has stepped into the shoes of the owner and therefore not entitled to any third-party compensation from the insured vehicle.
13. In the present case it has come in the evidence of PW1 that motorcycle in question was in the name of son of the deceased.

On behalf of insurance Simranpreet Kaur (R1W1) has appeared, who has testified that the vehicle in question was duly insured with it in the name of Suraj Mukhiya however it is stated that the insurance company is not liable to pay the compensation as vehicle was being driven in rash and negligent manner, insured entrusted the vehicle no.DL-5SCU-9535 to a person voluntarily and the deceased was not having any valid DL.

As such the vehicle was being used in violation of Section 149(2)(a)(ii) of M.V. Act.
14.
Having examined the evidence on the record, at the outset it be MACT No.484/2022 Digitally signed by Page 6 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK
Date: 2024.08.12 17:04:17 +0530 noted that deceased at the time of the accident was not the owner of the vehicle as registered owner of the vehicle/insured was his son.

Nothing has come in the evidence of PW1 to show that deceased had borrowed the motorcycle from his son and as such he stepped intro the shoes of owner in terms of judgment of N. Ningamma (supra) as noted above.

So far as the evidence of PW R1W1 regarding violation of terms are concerned, first of all even if the evidence of R1W1 is taken on the face of it,
liability of insurance company per se would exist to pay for third party risk as the deceased in this case was not the owner of the motorcycle in question.

Even otherwise I find substance in the submission of ld. Counsel for the petitioner when he submitted that the insurance policy also covered own risk that has been even admitted by R1W1 in cross examination that the vehicle was insured under bundled package and under the policy premium has been charged for personal accident cover of the owner/driver.
Counsel for the petitioner has rightly submitted that in view of the guidelines laid down by IRDAI every insurance policy for vehicle has to be for CPA cover.

Even if the policy in question was not comprehensive policy, still for the reasons and the law as noted above,
this Tribunal is of the considered view that for the death of the deceased in the road side accident,
insurance company is certainly liable to pay lump sum amount of compensation under Section 164 of M.V. Act.

Act.
Accordingly claim petition stands allowed.
Relief 17.
This Tribunal awards a lump sum compensation of Rs.5,00,000/- to the petitioner in terms of Section 164 of M.V. Act to be paid by respondent no.1/insurance company.

The respondent no.1 is directed to deposit the award amount in A/c no. 20780110171912 (IFSC Code UCBA0002078), UCO Bank, Karkardooma, Delhi, of PO MACT, Shahdara, through RTGS/ NEFT, within 30 days from today.
Respondent no.1 is also directed to give notice regarding deposit of the said amount to the petitioner.

The awarded amount is proportioned as under:
(i) A sum of Rs.2,50,000/- is directed to be released into the saving account of petitioner and balance amount of Rs.2,50,000/- is directed to be kept in fixed deposits of Rs.50,000/- each for a period of six months, one year, one and a half years, two years and two and a half years.
The amount of FDRs on maturity shall directly be released in petitioner's MACT Saving Bank Account.

The bank shall debit card(s) freeze the account of the claimant so that no debit card be issued in respect of the account of the claimant from any other branch of the bank.

21. File be consigned to Record Room.
